thesis: A basic calculator is judged by trust: every press visibly does the right thing, arithmetic is exact-looking, and nothing ever shows NaN or garbage.
job: enter digits and a decimal point (click or keyboard)
choose an operator (+ - x /) and see which is pending
enter second operand, see it on the display
press equals and read the result
chain operations (3 + 4 x 2 continues from the result)
repeat equals to reapply last operation
correct mistakes: backspace, clear entry, all clear
recover from error (divide by zero) without reload

principles: every press gives feedback within 100 ms
display is the single source of truth
steps: define states: entering first, operator pending, entering second, result shown, error
decide what each key does in each state
tricks: operator pressed twice replaces the first
percent relative to the left operand for + and -
tests: 5 / 0 shows an error and recovers on next digit

principles: operator keys distinct from digit keys
tricks: tabular numerals so digits do not jitter
tests: can a stranger tell it is a calculator in one glance
rapid typing never queues animation lag

tricks: aria-label for symbols: multiply, divide, minus

principles: one state object, one render function
pure compute function separate from DOM
tricks: round to 12 significant digits to kill float noise
keep operand as string while typing
toPrecision then Number to strip trailing zeros

parts: display with expression line and main number
expectations: long numbers do not overflow the display

kinds.name: pocket desk calculator
kinds.what: classic 4x5 keypad with big display and function keys; immediate-execution chaining

kinds.name: tape calculator
kinds.what: adding-machine style with scrolling paper history

kinds.name: expression calculator
kinds.what: type whole expression, shows running preview

descriptions: 4-column grid, 0 key may span two columns
expression line small above main number
digits neutral, operators tinted, equals strongest accent, clear keys muted red or grey

behaviors: digit after result starts new number
operator after result continues from result
operator right after operator replaces it
equals with no pending does nothing
percent: x/100, or x*left/100 with + or -
divide by zero shows Cannot divide by zero, next key resets

descriptions: use true math glyphs, not x and /

anti_keywords.instead: explicit state machine and pure compute
plain-language error message that clears on next key

anti_keywords.not: generic iOS clone with gradient orange circles
anti_keywords.instead: committed object-like design with its own character and tactile keys
scale font down by digit count, scroll expression line
full keyboard map: digits, + - * /, Enter, =, Backspace, Escape, ., %

checks: does 5 / 0 show an error and recover
does it work at 375 px wide
any external requests or console errors
